newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dasa offers Eurofighter price cut - paper.
newsitem.headline: Dasa offers Eurofighter price cut - paper.

text.p: Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG (Dasa) has offered to cut the price of the Eurofighter combat jet but has not yet convinced Germany's Defence Ministry to place a firm order, the Handelsblatt daily said on Monday.

The newspaper said Juergen Schrempp, chief executive of Dasa parent Daimler-Benz, met Defence Minister Volker Ruehe last week and offered to drop the total price of Germany's 180 Eurofighters to 23.3 billion marks from 26 billion marks.
But, Handelsblatt added, Schrempp failed to win a firm commitment from Ruehe to buy the Eurofighter -- a four-country project slated to start serial production next year.

Britain and Spain have both said they would place firm orders, putting Ruehe under pressure to follow suit. Ruehe and Dasa are still far apart on initial costs of production for the 21st century multi-purpose aircraft.

Handelsblatt said that Dasa -- which has a 30 percent stake in the Eurofighter consortium -- was seeking guaranteed payment of 6.9 billion marks by 2001. The German government is offering three billion marks less.
Germany's three-party centre-right governing coalition is squeezing the defence budget to try and get state finances into shape next year for European monetary union.

Finance Minister Theo Waigel said at the weekend there would be enough money for Eurofighter next year but junior coalition partners the Free Democrats (FDP) dismissed his comments as "an April fool's joke".

If the Eurofighter goes ahead, Dasa would have to pull out of the Franco-German satellite ventures Helios II and Horus -- despite pledges by Chancellor Helmut Kohl that the projects would go ahead, Handelsblatt said.
A decision on the satellite projects is expected at a summit next month.
British Aerospace has a 37.5 percent share in the Eurofighter project, Italy's Alenia 19.5 percent and Spain's Casa 13 percent.
